facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: Fortrea carries leverage that its earnings base supports only thinly, so creditors rely on liquidity and on maturities that begin to bite only in 2028 rather than on interest cover. At September 30, 2026 net debt was USD 834.7 million, which is 9.12x reported EBITDA for the last twelve months of USD 91.5 million, and that EBITDA covered cash interest 1.18x. The October 19, 2026 acquisition raises net debt to USD 873.7 million, or 9.55x, before any EBITDA the acquired business adds. rows.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view — paragraph 1
Chart data: revenue and EBITDA — paragraph 1

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- The issuer states no EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA or add-back schedule in any of the five filings, so EBITDA is derived for every period and no issuer-adjusted ratio or EBITDA bridge can be stated; this restricts leverage and coverage to a reported basis that carries restructuring and impairment charges, and because reported EBITDA was below zero in 2024, 2025 and the last twelve months to March 31, 2026, leverage is not calculable at those dates. Severity: High. Action: obtain the earnings releases or lender presentations that state adjusted EBITDA. - The issuer's reported Total Leverage Ratio, the interest coverage level and the covenant EBITDA definition are not printed in any filing, and the maximum leverage steps appear only in the 2024 annual report, so covenant headroom is not calculable at any date. Severity: High. Action: obtain the compliance certificates and the credit agreement. - The 2030 notes are called senior notes in the debt note and senior secured notes in the exhibit list and the liquidity discussion, and no source states their lien rank against the credit facilities or names the guarantors, so the security and ranking of USD 494.3 million of principal are Not supplied in the debt register and the notes are left out of the debt stack. Severity: High. Action: obtain the indenture and supplemental indenture. - No year-by-year principal schedule is printed at September 30, 2026, so the maturity ladder is drawn at December 31, 2025, and the 2029 line is a dash that is not read as zero. Severity: Low. Action: use the schedule in the next annual report. - Carrying value by instrument is not disclosed and discount and fees are one aggregate, so each instrument row carries principal and one financing cost adjustment row carries the difference. Severity: Low. - No fourth-quarter 2025 figures are printed, so the quarter is the year less nine months and assumes the nine-month 2025 comparative was not recast. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the 2025 quarterly reports. - The 2025 quarterly reports are not supplied, so the 2025 quarterly, half-year and nine-month columns are the comparatives printed in the 2026 reports and a recast cannot be tested; quarterly revenue ties across the three 2026 reports. Severity: Low. - The cash flow statements are year-to-date, so discrete second and third quarter cash flows are derived by difference and no 2025 discrete cash flow quarter is carried. Severity: Low. - The revolver availability at December 31, 2023 is not stated, so the 2023 undrawn facilities cell is Not supplied. Severity: Low. - Year 2022 statements printed in the 2024 annual report are not carried because the business was then part of Labcorp and no 2022 balance sheet is printed. Severity: Low. - Gross profit, interest income, maintenance and growth capital expenditure, funds from operations and per-share amounts are not carried: the statements do not print gross profit or a capital expenditure split, and funds from operations is not a measure the issuer states. Severity: Low. - Several statement lines are not printed in every filing: discontinued operations in the interim income statements, the 2026 interim lines for term loan and note proceeds, principal payments, share-settlement taxes and Former Parent transfers, and the discontinued operations lines on balance sheets after 2024; those cells are Not supplied rather than nil. Severity: Low. - The Applicable Margin, any interest floor and the exact maturity day of the 2030 notes are not stated in the filings read because they sit in the credit agreement and the indenture, which are not supplied, so those cells in the debt register are Not supplied. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the credit agreement and the indenture. - The 2023 backlog and largest-customer share are not stated in the filings read, 2022 revenue is not carried, and no prior last-twelve-month revenue is carried, so the matching cells of the KPI dashboard are Not supplied or not calculable. Severity: Low. - The acquisition of October 19, 2026 is a subsequent event kept out of period figures; the acquired business's EBITDA and debt are not stated, the deferred USD 4.0 million is not in net debt, and the purchase price allocation is not complete. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the next quarterly report.

facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: Fortrea is a single-segment clinical research provider spun out of Labcorp with no disclosed controlling holder, so creditors rely on management execution and customer demand rather than sponsor support, and that reliance looks fragile today. Backlog fell to USD 7.3 billion at September 30, 2026 after a USD 558 million reduction, one customer supplied 17.2% of nine-month revenue, and the finance chief role was disrupted by a court order in July 2026. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The business is a scaled but thin-margin services model: many contracts are fixed-price or fee-for-service with a cap, and more than a third of revenue is pass-through cost. Fortrea sells clinical development, clinical pharmacology and consulting services under full service, functional service provider and hybrid models, earned 47.35% of 2025 revenue in North America, 31.27% in Europe and 21.37% elsewhere, and passed through costs equal to 37.73% of revenue that earn no margin, leaving segment operating income at 3.21% of 2025 revenue. Margin is therefore set by staff utilisation and pricing discipline on the remaining work. tables.limitation: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The risk level is driven by turnover in the finance role and board entrenchment alongside an activist agreement, because those facts weaken reporting continuity and holder discipline, which implies closer monitoring of covenant certification and capital allocation. Countervailing evidence is the absence of dividends, repayment of debt from disposal proceeds, settled litigation and effective internal control. No sponsor is disclosed, so fund vintage, sponsor equity contribution and sponsor fees do not apply. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the credit agreement and the indenture.

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- Holdings, director independence and committee membership are not in the sources and the sources do not state whether Labcorp kept any shares after the spin, so the control and alignment of the board and the indemnity counterparty are not established. Severity: Minor. Action: Obtain the 2026 proxy statement and the registration statement. - The largest customer is not named, no contract term, renewal date or termination right is stated, revenue by delivery model, service and therapeutic area is not printed beyond one oncology share and no seasonal pattern is quantified, so concentration is sized by percentage only and the cause of the 2026 revenue decline rests on management wording. Severity: Minor. Action: Obtain customer disclosures, an earnings release or a lender presentation. - The reasons for the 2025 and 2026 officer changes, the August 2026 settlement terms and the June 2026 current report are not supplied, so the management stability view rests on dates and exhibit titles. Severity: Minor. Action: Obtain the current reports and their exhibits. - The acquired division's revenue, earnings, debt and purchase price allocation are not stated, and USD 41.0 million payable at closing is not reconciled with about USD 39.0 million paid in cash. Severity: Minor. Action: Use the next quarterly report. - No net new business award or book-to-bill figure is printed, so the USD 558 million backlog reduction cannot be split into attrition and estimation. Severity: Minor. Action: Obtain the earnings release. - The executed credit agreement, indenture and receivables purchase agreement are not supplied, so capacity under restricted payment, investment and lien baskets is not assessed, the subsidiary guarantors are named only as a class and the receivables agent's rating-change rights cannot be read. Severity: Material. Action: Obtain the executed documents. - No rating is supplied and the two agencies named in the receivables agreement are not identified, so the rating-change right cannot be sized. Severity: Minor. Action: Obtain rating reports. - Nothing dated after October 29, 2026 is supplied, so later events, including a third-quarter earnings release, cannot be excluded. Severity: Minor. Action: Obtain filings dated after October 29, 2026.

Reported EBITDA of USD 91.5 million gives net leverage of 9.12x and total debt leverage of 11.53x, and the house-adjusted measure that adds back restructuring, an Analyst Judgement, still gives 6.73x and 8.51x, with pro forma house-adjusted leverage not established; pro forma for the October 19, 2026 acquisition, net debt is USD 873.7 million, or 9.55x on reported EBITDA. Reported EBITDA covers cash interest of USD 77.8 million only 1.18x, and if the USD 150.0 million interest rate swap hedges the term loans, a 100 bp rise on the USD 422.00 million of floating debt it does not cover would add about USD 4.22 million of interest and cut cover to 1.12x. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Covenant headroom cannot be measured, but the stated compliance implies covenant EBITDA far above reported EBITDA, and the test tightens within weeks. The maximum Total Leverage Ratio is 5.75x at September 30, 2026, 5.50x at December 31, 2026, which is 43 days after the as-of date, and 5.30x after that; the issuer also says it must keep a net leverage and an interest coverage ratio and prints no level for the latter. If the test is on net debt, covenant EBITDA would need to be at least USD 145.17 million at 5.75x, USD 53.67 million above reported EBITDA, and USD 158.85 million at 5.50x on pro forma net debt of USD 873.7 million. The issuer states compliance and allows add-backs it does not print, so the gap is add-backs of unknown size; stock compensation of USD 50.80 million over the last twelve months added to house-adjusted EBITDA would bring net leverage to 4.78x. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_ftre-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Margins have improved through cost actions, but from a thin base and by a route that is less repeatable than volume growth. Segment operating income more than doubled to USD 108.7 million in nine months as selling and administrative costs fell, reported EBITDA reached USD 91.5 million over the last twelve months from USD 67.5 million at June 30, 2026, and the 3.43% EBITDA margin is thin because 37.28% of nine-month 2026 revenue is pass-through cost that earns nothing. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Pricing power is not evidenced. Many contracts are fixed-price or fee-for-service with a cap, which leaves cost overruns with Fortrea, customers can end most contracts on 30 to 90 days notice or internalise functional service provider resources, and management cites price competition as a risk. facts.label: PEST analysis
facts.text: Two factors are material to credit. Economic conditions matter because customers' research budgets and biotechnology funding set demand: management says biotechnology funding slowed in the first half of 2025 and strengthened in the second half, and forecasts research spending by large biopharmaceutical companies to grow about 4% to 5% a year over 2025 to 2030 while the contract research market grows more slowly in the short term, so demand is cyclical and a funding slowdown would show first in new awards and cancellations. Regulation matters because the industry is subject to extensive rules with penalties for violations, but the company states it is in compliance in all material respects and no regulatory proceeding is disclosed. Social and technological factors, including artificial intelligence investment, do not appear to be a primary credit driver on the evidence supplied. Cost and capex flexibility is average, since capital spending is 1.26% of revenue and selling costs have been cut, but personnel-heavy direct costs follow revenue down slowly. Margin stability is weak, with reported EBITDA negative in 2024 and 2025 and USD 91.5 million over the last twelve months.

facts.label: Financial profile and credit quality
facts.text: Free cash flow stability is weak, because USD 145.5 million of working capital inflow separates free cash flow of USD 169.0 million from USD 23.5 million before it. Ability to refinance is weak: leverage of 9.12x, maturities from June 30, 2028 and no sponsor, rating or price. Liquidity position is average: USD 668.3 million is ample for 12 months but the revolver ends with the term loan A maturity and its use depends on covenants. Financial policy and governance are average: conduct has favoured creditors, but the finance role has turned over and covenant relief was needed. The trend is improving from a low point, the main supports are liquidity, cost actions and contracted revenue, the main constraints are leverage, concentration and the 2028 wall, and the key missing datapoints are the covenant ratio and definition, the issuer's adjusted EBITDA, ratings and market prices. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C7

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Fortrea presents a weak business profile supported by liquidity of USD 668.3 million, cost actions that doubled segment operating income and USD 7.3 billion of backlog, but credit quality is constrained by net leverage of 9.12x reported EBITDA, a largest customer at 17.2% of revenue and free cash flow that depends on working capital. ## Request

Source readiness for Fortrea Holdings Inc. (issuer id ftre-1965040), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: five issuer filings (two annual reports and three quarterly reports) tested against the evidence needs of Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit, with the other modules of the pathway mapped for later runs.

No output from another module was supplied: Source readiness is the first module of this run.
## Findings
### Bottom line

The five Fortrea filings support Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit, but they carry no reported covenant ratios, guarantor and collateral terms or adjusted earnings, so creditors should treat covenant headroom and debt ranking as unverified. The set runs from the 2024 annual report to the quarterly report for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, signed 20 days before the run date, so it covers the October 2026 acquisition as a subsequent event but nothing filed afterwards.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 188–189; calculation C8

The main limits are the missing executed credit agreement, indenture and receivables purchase agreement, the missing 2026 proxy statement, the absence of any earnings release, rating, quote or peer data, and a label conflict over whether the 2030 notes are secured. The first limit keeps Legal & covenants blocked, and the others narrow Business & governance, Financial foundation and Fundamental credit without stopping them.

spans.text: # Financial foundation: Fortrea Holdings Inc.
## Request

Financial foundation for Fortrea Holdings Inc. (issuer id ftre-1965040), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: statements, debt, liquidity and period construction from the five issuer filings, with the balance sheet of 2026-09-30 as the latest and the acquisition of October 19, 2026 as a subsequent event.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_ftre-20241231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024 | 2025-03-03 | eaf3761841ef01594f1ab86c8bd6df9839eef8ec1710aee9a4c497b442e2780b | Balance sheet at 2023-12-31, the covenant steps of the February 28, 2025 amendment and the 2024 cross-check |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-02-26 | 8b95ed086bee1e22bdc9939204b714aadfab6b2aacd70a5ed5895da68a096d07 | Annual statements for 2025, 2024 and 2023, debt note and maturity schedule, supplemental cash flow information, segment note and exhibit list |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_ftre-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 | 2026-05-05 | 926245b69bc886e1bbe2a46da7bfe585969450fe165397cd69acf996b1d19ac1 | Q1 2026 statements with Q1 2025 comparatives and the 2026-03-31 balance sheet |

| 10-Q_2026-06-30_ftre-20260630.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 | 2026-07-29 | 9b87cb91036346612feecb02ecdb23500419e7f3968e1d881b6183bf42a2cff0 | Q2 2026 and six-month statements with 2025 comparatives and the 2026-06-30 balance sheet |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 | 2026-10-29 | c8421dd1a564dddecc236c5a1321482d1b190e3fb90be5f148bb69f7c89bdab4 | Latest statements, debt note, liquidity, receivables facility and the October 19, 2026 acquisition |
| Module | Handoff | sha256 | Use |

| Source readiness | CP-0 source readiness for Fortrea Holdings Inc. | 247198013151c6f841b8425725a60912d605fb02a7ccd66e4bfc2d95f1f3dfdd | Source coverage, period availability and the gaps it logged: no legal documents, no earnings release, no proxy statement, no 2025 quarterly reports |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Fortrea carries leverage that its earnings base supports only thinly, so creditors rely on liquidity and on maturities that begin to bite only in 2028 rather than on interest cover. At September 30, 2026 net debt was USD 834.7 million, which is 9.12x reported EBITDA for the last twelve months of USD 91.5 million, and that EBITDA covered cash interest 1.18x. The October 19, 2026 acquisition raises net debt to USD 873.7 million, or 9.55x, before any EBITDA the acquired business adds.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C3; calculation C8; calculation C15; calculation C16; calculation C21

Reported EBITDA carries restructuring charges, and a house-adjusted measure that adds them back, an Analyst Judgement, gives EBITDA of USD 124.0 million and net leverage of 6.73x. The issuer states no EBITDA, covenant ratio or maturity schedule for September 30, 2026, so covenant headroom is not established and the lien ranking of the 2030 notes rests on conflicting labels. Free cash flow of USD 169.0 million over the last twelve months leans on USD 145.5 million of working capital inflow.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 128–129; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 188; calculation C14; calculation C17; calculation C18; calculation C26
### Leverage and coverage

Reported EBITDA was negative in 2024 and 2025, at USD 76.6 million and USD 794.6 million below zero, so leverage on a reported basis has no meaning for either year; the 2025 figure carries a USD 797.9 million goodwill impairment. The recovery shows in the last twelve months: EBITDA rose from USD 67.5 million at June 30, 2026 to USD 91.5 million at September 30, 2026, while gross debt stayed at USD 1,055.3 million because no principal was repaid in nine months 2026. Leverage therefore moves only with earnings, and 11.53x total and 9.12x net remain high for a business whose cash interest was USD 77.8 million over the same twelve months.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 128–129; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–4; calculation C1; calculation C8; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C15

Cover of 1.18x at September 30, 2026 compares with 0.87x at June 30, 2026 and a negative cover in 2024 and 2025, so reported EBITDA now pays the interest but with little margin. Cash interest paid fell to USD 77.8 million over the last twelve months from USD 91.2 million in 2025, which the quarterly report attributes to the partial repurchase of the 2030 notes in 2025, no revolver borrowing and lower effective rates on the term loans; the rest of the improvement in cover is EBITDA.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 183; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C16; calculation C8; calculation C11
### Cash flow quality and funding float

Operating cash flow of USD 72.7 million in nine months 2026 exceeded the net loss of USD 36.2 million mainly because of non-cash charges, USD 59.4 million of depreciation and amortization and USD 36.0 million of stock compensation, while working capital added a net USD 12.7 million: unearned revenue added USD 51.0 million and payables USD 23.7 million, against USD 55.3 million absorbed by receivables. Unearned revenue stood at USD 525.5 million at September 30, 2026, a customer-funded float that reverses if new bookings slow, and a further USD 300.0 million of receivables are sold and kept off the balance sheet, so the debt lines understate the funding the business draws from outside them.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; calculation C26

Free cash flow of USD 169.0 million over the last twelve months, after USD 32.8 million of capital spending and after cash interest, is well above reported EBITDA of USD 91.5 million only because working capital contributed USD 145.5 million of the operating cash flow, USD 132.8 million of it in the fourth quarter of 2025; before working capital, free cash flow was USD 23.5 million. Operating cash flow of USD 262.8 million in 2024 was lifted in the same way by the sale of receivables under the receivables facility, which the 2025 annual report gives, with higher payments to suppliers, as the reason operating cash flow fell in 2025.

Basis: calculation C18; calculation C26; calculation C8; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 108; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 130; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4
### Liquidity and the October 2026 acquisition

Liquidity at September 30, 2026 was USD 220.6 million of cash plus USD 447.7 million available under the undrawn revolver, equal to 0.63x of total debt. The revolver and term loan A mature on June 30, 2028, when USD 387.5 million of term loan A falls due on the schedule at year-end 2025, and USD 649.0 million of notes and term loan B follow in 2030; the receivables facility is fully used and ends in February 2029. About USD 39.0 million of the cash left on October 19, 2026 for the acquisition, which is kept out of the period figures.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 164; calculation C19; calculation C21; calculation C24
### Data quality and definitions

The issuer states no EBITDA, so every EBITDA here is operating income plus depreciation and amortization, which includes restructuring and impairment charges; what the issuer's own definition would give is not established. A dash in a statement is carried as nil only where the printed totals confirm it. Depreciation and amortization in the 2024 cash flow statement of USD 86.9 million differs from USD 85.3 million in the income statement because the cash flow statement includes discontinued operations. Debt is the balance-sheet carrying value of USD 1,055.3 million, USD 11.0 million below contractual principal of USD 1,066.3 million, and the 2030 notes are labelled senior in the debt note and senior secured in the exhibit list.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 129–130; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 188; calculation C4
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a stressed reading is cash and time: cash rose by USD 46.0 million in nine months 2026 with nothing drawn on the revolver, and the first principal payment above USD 25.0 million falls in 2028. The evidence for it is that last-twelve-month free cash flow rests on working capital and on USD 51.0 million of unearned revenue growth in nine months, and that restructuring charges have recurred every year, so a slowdown in new business would remove the cash cushion before it lifted earnings.
Basis: calculation C18; calculation C26; calculation C24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 164

- The issuer's reported Total Leverage Ratio, the interest coverage level and the covenant EBITDA definition are not printed in any filing, and the maximum leverage steps appear only in the 2024 annual report, so covenant headroom is not calculable at any date. Severity: High. Action: obtain the compliance certificates and the credit agreement.

- The 2030 notes are called senior notes in the debt note and senior secured notes in the exhibit list and the liquidity discussion, and no source states their lien rank against the credit facilities or names the guarantors, so the security and ranking of USD 494.3 million of principal are Not supplied in the debt register and the notes are left out of the debt stack. - No year-by-year principal schedule is printed at September 30, 2026, so the maturity ladder is drawn at December 31, 2025, and the 2029 line is a dash that is not read as zero. Severity: Low. Action: use the schedule in the next annual report.

- Carrying value by instrument is not disclosed and discount and fees are one aggregate, so each instrument row carries principal and one financing cost adjustment row carries the difference. Severity: Low.

- No fourth-quarter 2025 figures are printed, so the quarter is the year less nine months and assumes the nine-month 2025 comparative was not recast. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the 2025 quarterly reports.

- The 2025 quarterly reports are not supplied, so the 2025 quarterly, half-year and nine-month columns are the comparatives printed in the 2026 reports and a recast cannot be tested; quarterly revenue ties across the three 2026 reports. Severity: Low.
- The cash flow statements are year-to-date, so discrete second and third quarter cash flows are derived by difference and no 2025 discrete cash flow quarter is carried. Severity: Low.
- The revolver availability at December 31, 2023 is not stated, so the 2023 undrawn facilities cell is Not supplied. Severity: Low.
- Year 2022 statements printed in the 2024 annual report are not carried because the business was then part of Labcorp and no 2022 balance sheet is printed. Severity: Low.

- Gross profit, interest income, maintenance and growth capital expenditure, funds from operations and per-share amounts are not carried: the statements do not print gross profit or a capital expenditure split, and funds from operations is not a measure the issuer states. Severity: Low.

- Several statement lines are not printed in every filing: discontinued operations in the interim income statements, the 2026 interim lines for term loan and note proceeds, principal payments, share-settlement taxes and Former Parent transfers, and the discontinued operations lines on balance sheets after 2024; those cells are Not supplied rather than nil. Severity: Low.

- The Applicable Margin, any interest floor and the exact maturity day of the 2030 notes are not stated in the filings read because they sit in the credit agreement and the indenture, which are not supplied, so those cells in the debt register are Not supplied. Severity: Low. Action: obtain the credit agreement and the indenture.

- The 2023 backlog and largest-customer share are not stated in the filings read, 2022 revenue is not carried, and no prior last-twelve-month revenue is carried, so the matching cells of the KPI dashboard are Not supplied or not calculable. Severity: Low.

- The acquisition of October 19, 2026 is a subsequent event kept out of period figures; the acquired business's EBITDA and debt are not stated, the deferred USD 4.0 million is not in net debt, and the purchase price allocation is not complete. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the next quarterly report.

spans.text: # Business & governance: Fortrea Holdings Inc.
## Request

Business & governance for Fortrea Holdings Inc. (issuer id ftre-1965040), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business model, transactions, ownership and control, operating model, history and governance behaviour from the five issuer filings and the source readiness review, with the October 19, 2026 acquisition treated as a subsequent event.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_ftre-20241231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024 | 2025-03-03 | eaf3761841ef01594f1ab86c8bd6df9839eef8ec1710aee9a4c497b442e2780b | Business and customer concentration for 2024, backlog and obligations at 2024-12-31, the spin-off, the February 21, 2025 cooperation agreement with Starboard Value LP and the February 28, 2025 credit amendment |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-02-26 | 8b95ed086bee1e22bdc9939204b714aadfab6b2aacd70a5ed5895da68a096d07 | Base report: business, services, customers, backlog, risk factors on control and the former parent, rights plan, debt and receivables notes, segment note, exhibit list and the deferral of Part III to a proxy statement |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_ftre-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 | 2026-05-05 | 926245b69bc886e1bbe2a46da7bfe585969450fe165397cd69acf996b1d19ac1 | Backlog and obligations at 2026-03-31, the rights plan before expiry and the chief financial officer's signature of May 5, 2026 |

| 10-Q_2026-06-30_ftre-20260630.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 | 2026-07-29 | 9b87cb91036346612feecb02ecdb23500419e7f3968e1d881b6183bf42a2cff0 | The July 2026 lawsuit over the chief financial officer's appointment, the restraining order, the interim officer, the rights plan expiry and backlog at 2026-06-30 |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 | 2026-10-29 | c8421dd1a564dddecc236c5a1321482d1b190e3fb90be5f148bb69f7c89bdab4 | Latest operating data, backlog reduction, customer concentration, settlement and dismissal of litigation, October 23, 2026 compensation decisions and the October 19, 2026 acquisition |
| Module | Handoff | sha256 | Use |

| Source readiness | CP-0 source readiness for Fortrea Holdings Inc. | 247198013151c6f841b8425725a60912d605fb02a7ccd66e4bfc2d95f1f3dfdd | Source coverage and period availability, and the gaps it logged: no legal documents, no 2026 proxy statement, no earnings release, rating or peer data |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Fortrea is a single-segment clinical research provider spun out of Labcorp with no disclosed controlling holder, so creditors rely on management execution and customer demand rather than sponsor support, and that reliance looks fragile today. Backlog fell to USD 7.3 billion at September 30, 2026 after a USD 558 million reduction, one customer supplied 17.2% of nine-month revenue, and the finance chief role was disrupted by a court order in July 2026.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_ftre-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C3; calculation C5

Sponsor and governance risk is Medium: the filings show no dividend, notes repurchased under an asset sale covenant and a covenant amendment bought with a fee, but also an activist cooperation agreement, a staggered board until 2028 and compensation changes approved while backlog was being written down. The evidence supports caution on management stability, not a finding of creditor-adverse conduct.
### Key findings

The business is a scaled but thin-margin services model: many contracts are fixed-price or fee-for-service with a cap, and more than a third of revenue is pass-through cost. Fortrea sells clinical development, clinical pharmacology and consulting services under full service, functional service provider and hybrid models, earned 47.35% of 2025 revenue in North America, 31.27% in Europe and 21.37% elsewhere, and passed through costs equal to 37.73% of revenue that earn no margin, leaving segment operating income at 3.21% of 2025 revenue. Margin is therefore set by staff utilisation and pricing discipline on the remaining work.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 79; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 152; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 184; calculation C8; calculation C16

Contracted revenue visibility is thinning faster than reported revenue. Remaining performance obligations fell 5.21% to USD 4,390.7 million between December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2026, and the share due within 12 months slipped from 29.3% to 26%, so revenue expected over the next 12 months from them is about USD 1,142 million, about 16% lower than at year end and about 43% of last twelve months revenue of USD 2,666.7 million. Most contracts can be ended on 30 to 90 days notice, so the USD 7.3 billion of backlog is a pipeline, not a claim on cash.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 153; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C4

Underlying activity is steadier than the revenue line and margins have improved, but from a thin base. Nine-month revenue fell 2.7% to USD 2,006.2 million, yet USD 48.3 million of the USD 56.7 million decline is lower pass-through costs that earn no margin, so revenue excluding them slipped only 0.66%. Segment operating income more than doubled to USD 108.7 million from USD 54.0 million, helped by segment selling and administrative costs that fell 9.33% and by restructuring plans approved in the fourth quarters of 2024 and 2025.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; calculation C2; calculation C9

Customer concentration is the largest business risk to creditors, and it rose through 2025. One customer was 18.1% of 2025 revenue, against two at 14.3% and 10.5% in 2024, the top twenty customers reached 69% of revenue from 61% in 2023, and the largest customer was 17.2% of nine-month 2026 revenue and 18.5% of receivables at September 30, 2026. If its revenue earned the company-average contribution of 20.05%, losing it would remove about USD 69.20 million of contribution, 2.62x nine-month operating income of USD 26.4 million, an Analyst Judgement that overstates the loss to the extent the customer's revenue is pass-through.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 140; 10-K_2024-12-31_ftre-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2024-12-31_ftre-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7

Working capital is funded by customers and by a receivables sale that is fully used, so cash conversion depends on award flow and on the lender's rights after a rating change. Unearned revenue of USD 525.5 million is 2.38x cash of USD 220.6 million and has risen from USD 214.2 million at the end of 2023, and USD 300.0 million of receivables are sold, 46.79% of those still on the balance sheet. The February 24, 2026 amendment moved the facility's end to February 23, 2029 but gives the administrative agent rights after an adverse rating change by either of two agencies.

Ownership is dispersed public equity with no disclosed controlling holder, so no sponsor stands behind creditors, yet the board is protected against takeover and has already been pressed by an activist. The board is divided into three classes until the 2028 annual meeting, charter amendments need 75% approval until then, and a rights plan with a 10% trigger ran from June 11, 2025 until it expired on June 10, 2026 without extension. A February 21, 2025 cooperation agreement gave Starboard Value LP a say in board composition. Holdings, director independence and committee membership are not established in the sources.

Management stability is the weakest governance point. The chief financial officer role passed from Jill McConnell, who signed the quarterly report of May 2026, to Jason Knoblauch, whose appointment a prior employer challenged in court on July 6, 2026; a restraining order on July 25 led the board to name director David R. Smith interim chief financial officer from July 27, and Mr. Knoblauch signed the September report as chief financial officer after a settlement in August with no material impact. On October 23, 2026 the compensation committee approved reimbursement of private aviation for the chief executive of up to 50 flight hours a year, capped at USD 300,000, and accepted Mr. Knoblauch's waiver of a USD 1,250,000 cash inducement award in return for legal fee indemnity and the lapse of forfeiture provisions on his earlier pay.

Creditor treatment since the spin has been conservative on cash leaving the company, but leverage was set by the separation and covenant relief carried a price. Fortrea incurred USD 1,640.0 million of term loans and notes at the spin and paid USD 1,595.0 million, 97.26% of that, to Labcorp; since then it has paid no dividend, paid down USD 482.7 million of term loans in 2024 and repurchased USD 75.7 million of notes in the fourth quarter of 2025 under the indenture's asset sale covenant. The February 28, 2025 amendment raised the maximum Total Leverage Ratio to 6.00x for quarters through June 30, 2026, then 5.75x at September 30, 2026, 5.50x at December 31, 2026 and 5.30x after, in return for a lender fee and extra limits on investments, restricted payments and liens during the adjustment period.

Acquisition appetite is modest on the evidence: the only purchase the filings describe since the spin is the USD 45.0 million Early Phase Services division of Worldwide Clinical Trials, bought on October 19, 2026, with about USD 39.0 million paid in cash from cash on hand, 17.68% of September 30 cash, and USD 4.0 million deferred. One small cash deal does not establish a pattern, and the 2024 disposal of Enabling Services for USD 340.0 million narrowed the business to one segment rather than adding leverage.

Disclosure is adequate for monitoring in the audited statements but inconsistent on points creditors price. The annual report says the company has no off-balance sheet financing other than short term leases and letters of credit, yet it had sold USD 300.0 million of receivables that were removed from the balance sheet, and the 2030 notes are called senior notes in the debt note but senior secured notes in the liquidity discussion. The auditor reported on internal control over financial reporting, which management concluded was effective at December 31, 2025.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against caution is operating momentum and the absence of creditor-adverse conduct. Segment operating income more than doubled in nine months, backlog of USD 7.3 billion is still 2.74x last twelve months revenue, management states that the USD 558 million reduction reflected scope and delivery estimates and not any recent material customer communication and expects no material effect on near-term revenue, the company reported compliance with all covenants at September 30, 2026, and the court case over the finance chief settled with no material impact while the securities class action was dismissed with prejudice on September 28, 2026. No dividend has been paid and the only acquisition was small and paid in cash.

The view would improve if the next quarterly report shows backlog stabilising and the share of obligations due within 12 months back above 29.3%, if the largest customer's share of revenue falls without a loss of revenue, and if the proxy statement shows independent directors and no holder above 10%. It would worsen if backlog falls again, if the largest customer cuts or ends work, if the receivables agent's rating-change rights are triggered, or if the finance chief role changes hands again.
### Limitations

- The Medium sponsor and governance rating assumes no holder with influence beyond the activist agreement, but the sources print no holdings, director independence or committee structure, so a holder near the 10% level that triggered the former rights plan would raise the risk level.

- The concentration finding rests on percentages alone: no customer is named and no contract term, renewal date or termination right is stated, so a long-dated contract with the largest customer would lower the risk and a near-term expiry would raise it.

- Revenue by delivery model and by therapeutic area is not printed beyond one oncology share, so the statement that weaker functional service provider demand drives the decline rests on management wording and could prove wrong.

- The reasons for the 2025 and 2026 officer changes, the August 2026 settlement terms and the June 2026 current report are not in the sources, so the management stability finding rests on dates and exhibit titles and could be harsher or milder once they are read.
- The acquired division's revenue, earnings and purchase price allocation are not stated, so whether the October 2026 deal changes the operating model or adds earnings is not established.

- Backlog is defined by management and no net new business or book-to-bill figure is printed, so whether the USD 558 million adjustment signals customer attrition rather than estimation is not established; attrition would lower the view on revenue visibility further.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The founding transaction is the June 30, 2023 spin-off from Labcorp, a pro-rata distribution of one Fortrea share for each Labcorp share. Fortrea incurred USD 1,640.0 million of term loans and notes at the spin, namely USD 570.0 million of 7.50% senior notes due 2030 issued on June 27, 2023, a USD 500.0 million first lien term loan A due 2028 and a USD 570.0 million first lien term loan B due 2030, alongside a USD 450.0 million revolving facility, and it paid USD 1,595.0 million to Labcorp. The separation agreement leaves Fortrea responsible for substantially all liabilities of its business and for the Labcorp obligations it assumed, Labcorp has indemnified Fortrea for certain liabilities without assurance that the indemnity will suffice, and the transition services agreement ended on June 30, 2025.

Two later transactions reshaped the balance sheet. The sale of the Enabling Services segment to Endeavor Buyer LLC, an affiliate of Arsenal Capital Partners, was agreed on March 9, 2024 and closed in the second quarter of 2024 for USD 340.0 million, of which USD 295.0 million was paid at closing and USD 45.0 million arrived as milestone payments of USD 20.0 million in the first quarter of 2025 and USD 25.0 million in the third quarter of 2025. The company paid down USD 70.2 million of term loan A and USD 412.5 million of term loan B in 2024 and repurchased USD 75.7 million of the notes in the fourth quarter of 2025 under the indenture's asset sale covenant, leaving USD 494.3 million outstanding. Funding also comes from a three-year USD 300.0 million receivables securitisation entered on May 6, 2024 and amended on February 24, 2026 to end on February 23, 2029; it is fully used and gives the administrative agent rights after an adverse rating change by either of two agencies.

The only transaction after the latest balance sheet is the October 19, 2026 acquisition of the Early Phase Services division of Worldwide Clinical Trials for about USD 45.0 million: USD 41.0 million payable at closing and USD 4.0 million deferred until transition services end and no later than 12 months after closing, with about USD 39.0 million paid in cash from cash on hand and the purchase price allocation not yet complete. The filings show no new debt issue after the spin: financing cash flows were nil in the nine months to September 30, 2026 and revolving borrowings of USD 453.9 million in 2025 were repaid in the same year. The February 28, 2025 amendment raised the maximum Total Leverage Ratio to 6.00x for quarters through June 30, 2026, with step-downs to 5.75x, 5.50x and 5.30x, in return for a lender fee and extra limits on investments, restricted payments and liens during the adjustment period.

- The acquired division's revenue, earnings, debt and purchase price allocation are not stated, and USD 41.0 million payable at closing is not reconciled with about USD 39.0 million paid in cash. Severity: Minor. Action: Use the next quarterly report.

- No net new business award or book-to-bill figure is printed, so the USD 558 million backlog reduction cannot be split into attrition and estimation. Severity: Minor. Action: Obtain the earnings release.

- The executed credit agreement, indenture and receivables purchase agreement are not supplied, so capacity under restricted payment, investment and lien baskets is not assessed, the subsidiary guarantors are named only as a class and the receivables agent's rating-change rights cannot be read. Severity: Material. Action: Obtain the executed documents.
- No rating is supplied and the two agencies named in the receivables agreement are not identified, so the rating-change right cannot be sized. Severity: Minor. Action: Obtain rating reports.

- Nothing dated after October 29, 2026 is supplied, so later events, including a third-quarter earnings release, cannot be excluded. Severity: Minor. Action: Obtain filings dated after October 29, 2026.

spans.text: # Fundamental credit: Fortrea Holdings Inc.
## Request

Fundamental credit for Fortrea Holdings Inc. (issuer id ftre-1965040), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the overall credit profile, strongest support and primary downside path from the five issuer filings and the supplied readiness, financial and business analyses, with the October 19, 2026 acquisition treated as a subsequent event.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_ftre-20241231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024 | 2025-03-03 | eaf3761841ef01594f1ab86c8bd6df9839eef8ec1710aee9a4c497b442e2780b | Covenant steps of the February 28, 2025 amendment, 2024 backlog and customer concentration, and the spin-off terms |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-02-26 | 8b95ed086bee1e22bdc9939204b714aadfab6b2aacd70a5ed5895da68a096d07 | Business, markets and competition, risk factors, debt maturities and covenants, cash flow statement, segment note, pension and exhibit list |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_ftre-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 | 2026-05-05 | 926245b69bc886e1bbe2a46da7bfe585969450fe165397cd69acf996b1d19ac1 | Backlog and obligations at 2026-03-31 and quarterly comparatives |

| Module | Handoff | sha256 | Use |

| Source readiness | CP-0 source readiness for Fortrea Holdings Inc. | 247198013151c6f841b8425725a60912d605fb02a7ccd66e4bfc2d95f1f3dfdd | Source coverage and the gaps it logged: no legal documents, proxy statement, earnings release, rating or peer data |

| Financial foundation | CP-1 financial foundation for Fortrea Holdings Inc. | 374fd418135702cf0906278cc27afe524ce806beb7c7be7018ef2e45d34ff990 | Leverage, coverage, cash flow, liquidity, debt stack, maturity ladder and the post-balance-sheet adjustment for the October 19, 2026 acquisition |

## Findings
### Bottom line

Fortrea's fundamental credit is weak: net debt of USD 834.7 million at September 30, 2026 is 9.12x last twelve months reported EBITDA, so creditors rely on liquidity and a 2028 refinancing rather than on cash flow. Pro forma for the October 19, 2026 acquisition, net debt is USD 873.7 million, or 9.55x.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C1

The strongest support is liquidity of USD 668.3 million before the acquisition's cash payment, with only scheduled amortization of up to USD 25.0 million a year before June 30, 2028. The weakest points are one customer at 17.2% of revenue, backlog cut to USD 7.3 billion and free cash flow of USD 23.5 million before USD 145.5 million of working capital inflow. The primary downside path is loss of work from the largest customer, which would remove contribution of about USD 91.98 million, roughly all of reported EBITDA of USD 91.5 million.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C5; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C9
### Key findings

Leverage is the binding constraint, and even the house-adjusted measure leaves it high. Reported EBITDA of USD 91.5 million gives net leverage of 9.12x and total debt leverage of 11.53x, and the house-adjusted measure that adds back restructuring, an Analyst Judgement, still gives 6.73x and 8.51x, with pro forma house-adjusted leverage not established; pro forma for the October 19, 2026 acquisition, net debt is USD 873.7 million, or 9.55x on reported EBITDA. Reported EBITDA covers cash interest of USD 77.8 million only 1.18x, and if the USD 150.0 million interest rate swap hedges the term loans, a 100 bp rise on the USD 422.00 million of floating debt it does not cover would add about USD 4.22 million of interest and cut cover to 1.12x.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; calculation C1; calculation C4

Covenant headroom cannot be measured, but the stated compliance implies covenant EBITDA far above reported EBITDA, and the test tightens within weeks. The maximum Total Leverage Ratio is 5.75x at September 30, 2026, 5.50x at December 31, 2026, which is 43 days after the as-of date, and 5.30x after that; the issuer also says it must keep a net leverage and an interest coverage ratio and prints no level for the latter. If the test is on net debt, covenant EBITDA would need to be at least USD 145.17 million at 5.75x, USD 53.67 million above reported EBITDA, and USD 158.85 million at 5.50x on pro forma net debt of USD 873.7 million. The issuer states compliance and allows add-backs it does not print, so the gap is add-backs of unknown size; stock compensation of USD 50.80 million over the last twelve months added to house-adjusted EBITDA would bring net leverage to 4.78x.
Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_ftre-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 96; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C3

Free cash flow is not a dependable source of repayment. Last twelve months free cash flow of USD 169.0 million, after USD 32.8 million of capital spending and USD 77.8 million of cash interest, includes USD 145.5 million of working capital inflow, USD 132.8 million of it in the fourth quarter of 2025, so free cash flow before working capital is USD 23.5 million, 25.68% of reported EBITDA. Customers and a receivables sale fund the business from outside the debt, with unearned revenue of USD 525.5 million and USD 300.0 million of receivables sold, and cash taxes of USD 14.50 million are paid despite pre-tax losses.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 183; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation C5

Revenue visibility is thinning and rests on few customers, which makes it the primary operating risk. Remaining performance obligations fell 5.21% to USD 4,390.7 million at September 30, 2026, backlog fell to USD 7.3 billion after a USD 558 million reduction, and the revenue contracted for the next 12 months is about USD 1,142 million, about 43% of last twelve months revenue. One customer was 17.2% of nine-month revenue and the top twenty were 69% of 2025 revenue, while most contracts can be ended on 30 to 90 days notice.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C8

Margins have improved through cost actions, but from a thin base and by a route that is less repeatable than volume growth. Segment operating income more than doubled to USD 108.7 million in nine months as selling and administrative costs fell, reported EBITDA reached USD 91.5 million over the last twelve months from USD 67.5 million at June 30, 2026, and the 3.43% EBITDA margin is thin because 37.28% of nine-month 2026 revenue is pass-through cost that earns nothing. Restructuring charges have recurred every year, USD 44.1 million in 2025 and USD 10.1 million in nine months 2026, so part of the saving was bought with cash charges.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 105; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C10

Liquidity is adequate for the next 12 months but does not cover the 2028 maturities without a refinancing. Cash of USD 220.6 million and USD 447.7 million of undrawn revolver give USD 668.3 million before the acquisition's cash payment, which Financial foundation does not carry into pro forma cash; USD 387.5 million of term loan A and the USD 450.0 million revolver fall due on June 30, 2028, about 19 months away, and cash is 0.57x the term loan A balance. The revolver and term loan A enter their final 12 months on June 30, 2027, USD 649.0 million follows in 2030, and no rating, price or sponsor is supplied to show whether the market will refinance a business at this leverage.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 164; calculation C7

Financial policy has been creditor-friendly in conduct but brings no outside support. No sponsor stands behind the debt, no dividend has been paid, USD 75.7 million of notes were repurchased from disposal proceeds under the indenture and covenant relief in 2025 was paid for with a lender fee and extra limits on investments, restricted payments and liens. Governance risk is Medium on the evidence, driven by turnover in the finance role in 2026 and an activist agreement, not by any creditor-adverse action.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 163; 10-K_2024-12-31_ftre-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 96; calculation C11

Claims outside reported debt and the quality of the balance sheet widen the leverage picture. Adding the USD 300.0 million of receivables sold to net debt of USD 834.7 million, which is USD 873.7 million pro forma for the October 19, 2026 acquisition, gives USD 1,134.7 million, or 12.40x reported EBITDA and 9.15x house-adjusted EBITDA; operating leases add USD 63.1 million, the UK pension plan has a small funding surplus, and goodwill and intangibles of USD 1,521.9 million exceed equity of USD 532.3 million.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11–12; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 179; calculation C6
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a weak view is recovery and time. Reported EBITDA rose from USD 67.5 million at June 30, 2026 to USD 91.5 million at September 30, 2026, cash rose by USD 46.0 million in nine months with no revolver borrowing, house-adjusted net leverage fell to 6.73x from 18.53x at the end of 2025, before any effect of the acquisition, backlog of USD 7.3 billion is still 2.74x last twelve months revenue, the issuer states compliance with all covenants at September 30, 2026 and no principal above USD 25.0 million falls due before 2028. Capital spending of 1.26% of nine-month revenue also leaves little to fund, so a stable top line would let cost savings reach cash.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C2; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C10

The view would improve if the fourth-quarter report shows backlog stabilising, free cash flow before working capital rising above USD 23.5 million without a further working capital inflow, the issuer printing its covenant ratio with headroom at the 5.50x and 5.30x steps, and an extension of the 2028 maturities. It would worsen if the largest customer cuts work, if unearned revenue falls below USD 525.5 million, if the receivables agent's rating-change rights are triggered, or if the 2028 maturities remain unaddressed when they enter the 12-month window on June 30, 2027.
### Limitations

- The covenant requirement of USD 145.17 million of EBITDA at 5.75x assumes a net debt test and no netting limits, so a gross debt test or a different EBITDA definition would move the implied add-backs and could show real headroom or none.

- The issuer states no EBITDA and no guidance, so leverage rests on derived and house-adjusted measures; an issuer-adjusted figure above USD 124.0 million would lower leverage and weaken the conclusion that no supported measure removes it.

- The downside scenario halves the largest customer's work and holds selling costs fixed, both assumptions without a management plan to test them, so the contribution lost, USD 45.99 million, could be materially higher or lower.

- No rating, share price, bond quote or peer data is supplied, so the refinancing conclusion is not tested against market pricing, and a par-priced bond or a strong equity value would lower the 2028 refinancing risk.

- The last twelve months free cash flow depends on a fourth-quarter 2025 working capital inflow whose reversal or repeat in the fourth quarter of 2026 is not visible, so the finding that cash flow is undependable could change with the year-end report.
- The interest rate swap's maturity and the loans it hedges are not stated, so the 100 bp sensitivity of USD 4.22 million could be understated if the swap expires or the notional covers other debt.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Liquidity is the strongest support. Cash of USD 220.6 million and an undrawn USD 447.7 million revolver, with USD 2.3 million of letters of credit, give USD 668.3 million, before the acquisition's cash payment that Financial foundation does not carry into pro forma cash, which is 6.04x a year of cash interest and capital spending together, and nothing was repaid or drawn in nine months 2026. That means debt service through 2027 does not depend on a refinancing, which lowers near-term default risk as long as the revolver stays available.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C7

Cost actions have lifted margin, and low capital intensity lets the gain reach cash. Segment operating income of USD 108.7 million in nine months is 101.30% above the prior year and selling and administrative costs fell 9.33%, while capital spending is 1.26% of revenue, so if volume holds the saving converts to cash that can repay debt, although restructuring recurs every year.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C10

Contracted revenue gives time to adjust. Backlog of USD 7.3 billion is 2.74x last twelve months revenue and remaining performance obligations are USD 4,390.7 million, so a downturn would work through the income statement over several quarters, not at once, which gives management room to cut cost before covenants tighten, although most contracts can be ended on 30 to 90 days notice.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation C8

Conduct has favoured creditors. No dividend has been paid, USD 75.7 million of notes were repurchased from disposal proceeds under the indenture and the 2024 term loan paydown was USD 482.7 million, so cash has stayed in the business, which supports deleveraging if earnings hold; the absence of a sponsor means no leakage but also no equity support.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 163; calculation C11

Leverage against earnings is the weakest point. Net debt of USD 834.7 million is 9.12x reported EBITDA of USD 91.5 million (USD 873.7 million and 9.55x pro forma for the October 19, 2026 acquisition) and cover of cash interest is 1.18x, so a small fall in earnings removes interest cover and tightens covenant tests that step down to 5.50x at December 31, 2026 and 5.30x after.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2024-12-31_ftre-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 96; calculation C1; calculation C3

Customer concentration makes earnings fragile. One customer was 17.2% of nine-month revenue and the top twenty were 69% of 2025 revenue, and because selling costs are largely fixed the loss of the largest customer's work would remove about USD 91.98 million of contribution, which is roughly all of reported EBITDA, an Analyst Judgement that overstates the loss to the extent the revenue is pass-through.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C8; calculation C9

Free cash flow depends on working capital. Last twelve months free cash flow of USD 169.0 million includes USD 145.5 million of working capital inflow and is USD 23.5 million before it, so repayment capacity from operations is small and a reversal of the USD 525.5 million of unearned revenue would draw on cash.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C5

The 2028 maturities and the covenant step-downs create a refinancing event. USD 387.5 million of term loan A and the USD 450.0 million revolver fall due on June 30, 2028 and cash is 0.57x the term loan A balance, so the business must refinance or extend at a leverage that the covenant steps and the absence of a sponsor, rating or price make hard to place.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 164; 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation C7

Contracted revenue is eroding. Remaining performance obligations fell 5.21% in nine months and revenue contracted for the next 12 months is about 16% lower than at year end, so earnings could soften before the cost actions run out, and management turnover in the finance role adds execution risk at the point when lenders need reliable reporting.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_ftre-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_ftre-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 153; calculation C8
